subject: forestSpirit
pitch: A small forest spirit, part deer and part mossy stone. A body of grey river stone covered in soft green moss, slender wooden legs ending in little hooves, branching antlers sprouting tiny white flowers and leaves, a pale wooden mask-like face with two glowing green eyes, and a few fireflies circling its head.
reasoning:
I'm planning a small deer spirit model, around 0.9m tall with antlers reaching 1.1m, facing forward. I'm sketching out the skeleton structure—root, spine chain, neck, head, jaw, four legs, tail, and antlers—using the joint and chain API to define each part safely.

Now I'm working out exact coordinates: a faceted stone-like boulder body as an ellipsoid, wooden legs placed at specific hip/knee/hock/tip positions using polyline chains, swept with varying radii, and hooves modeled as small cylinders at each foot's base touching the ground.

I'm mirroring the leg setup for left/right sides and defining a spine chain of joints running from tail to head, parented to a root joint positioned at the body's base, so the rigid body meshes can attach to the skeleton correctly.

Still defining the skeleton...

Adding skull details and eye sockets...

Planning the antler geometry using a curved sweep through a few control points with tapering radius, checking the overall height feels proportionate for a small deer, and deciding to scale the tines down slightly before branching off secondary tines from the main beam points.

I'm writing a helper function that generates each tine as a tapered capsule shape branching from points along the antler beam, then capping the tips with small white flower spheres.

Adding flower petals and leaves...

Now I'm thinking about the body paint texture, blending stone-grey tones with moss green highlights along the top using a countershade pattern.

Nesting countershade with moss and stone works fine together. For moss tufts, I'll skip textured cards and instead scatter small flattened spheres across the body surface using the surface scatter method, sticking them with embedding so the geometry can be shared across instances without issue.

I'm adding a shoulder boulder as a second stone sphere, plus the main body composed of an ellipsoid for the torso, rump, and chest, all painted with the same baked texture sheet to keep things consistent. For the tail I'm setting up a simple joint chain with a small moss-covered tuft at the tip.

Now I'm building the actual tail chain with two joints, assigning it the "tail" role with a tapered wood sweep radius and a mossy tuft finish. I'm defining the role system for all the chains—spine, neck, legs, tail, head, jaw—so each joint type behaves consistently. Then I'm adding a ring of five small pale-yellow glowing firefly spheres circling around the head at varying heights for a bit of magical ambiance.

I'm parenting the fireflies to the root joint so they circle freely rather than being tied to the head, building each one as a small glowing body sphere with two tiny flattened white wing spheres. I'm also scattering a few simple white flowers with yellow centers across the mossy body using flattened petal shapes, filtered to only appear on upward-facing surfaces.

Now I'm defining wood grain textures for the legs and head using paired brown and tan tones, darker grain for the antlers, and a dark near-black color for the hooves.

For leg anatomy, I'm placing hoof cylinders at ground level with the leg tip joint at y=0.05, setting up a four-point chain per leg (hip, knee, ankle, hoof) to form three spans, with front/hind and left/right naming conventions for each joint.

Now I'm checking that the leg attachment points at x=0.12 sit within the body ellipsoid's surface at that height, confirming they're properly embedded, then laying out specific coordinates for the front and hind leg joint chains.

Next I'm working out the neck geometry: a two-span sweep from the base at spine2 up to the head position, tapering the radius along its length, then setting up the spine joint chain with three points and attaching the neck as a child of the second spine joint.

Moving to the head joint, parented to the second neck segment with a slight forward tilt, and a jaw joint parented to the head for later mouth articulation. For the ears, I'm placing small scaled spheres above the head, angled outward with opposite z-rotations so they flare symmetrically left and right, painted in the same wood tone as the rest of the fur.

For facial detail I'm adding subtle dark markings around the eyes and nose plus a moss tuft on top of the head to anchor the antler bases. Now I'm defining the antler geometry as a branching beam with multiple capsule segments for the tines, building out the coordinates for each branch point symmetrically for left and right sides.

Adding flower petals using shared sphere geometries, keeping antler part counts well under the limit, and setting up leaves as scaled unit spheres with randomized rotation placed along the tines.

I'm scattering moss clumps and small flowers across the body's upward-facing surfaces, alternating greens and filtering by normal direction, then arranging fireflies in a ring near the top of the creature.

I'm skipping translucent glow halos since opacity isn't available, opting instead for small glowing spheres with dark socket eyes for contrast, then finalizing the structure to export the root.

Still writing body geometry...
